deliverable.executive_summary: This report provides a thorough market and needs analysis for the PANORAIMA project. PANORAIMA aims to develop a forward-looking, human-centred AI educational programme across four key societal sectors: Healthcare and Lifesciences, Law and Compliance, Media and Culture, and Management and Finances. Drawing on qualitative and quantitative data collected from over 100 stakeholders across 10 European countries, the report outlines the current landscape of AI adoption, identifies skill gaps, maps sector-specific needs, and assesses preferred training formats and job profiles. The findings are also contextualised within EU policy frameworks such as the AI Act and GDPR. Key insights include: • High AI Uptake: Over 90% of large enterprises and SMEs surveyed are already using or exploring AI technologies. However, challenges persist, including regulatory complexity, legacy systems, lack of trust, and internal capacity gaps. • Diverging Skill Demands: Sectors such as Healthcare and Lifesciences and Management and Finance prioritise technical skills (e.g., ML, cloud computing, validation of AI systems), while Law and Compliance and Media and Culture stress non-technical competencies (e.g., AI ethics, governance, explainability). • Cross-Sectoral Gaps: Common needs include AI literacy, prompt engineering, risk management, ethical awareness, and data governance. The demand is strongest for professionals who combine technical proficiency with human-centric, regulatory, and ethical knowledge and skills. • Preferred Learning Formats: Stakeholders express a clear preference for flexible, modular, hybrid training approaches that accommodate full-time professionals and are aligned with real-world roles and time constraints. • Emerging Job Roles: New hybrid roles are emerging (e.g., AI Risk Manager, Clinical AI Analyst, AI Media Curator), suggesting that the future workforce must be π-shaped—combining deep domain expertise with applied AI fluency and cross-functional insight. • Ethical and Inclusion Challenges: There is a pronounced need to address issues like bias, transparency, accountability, and sustainability in AI systems. Gaps persist in practical ethics training, inclusive design, accessibility, and environmental awareness (e.g., “Green AI”).
